quarterly_data.signal: The US FDA approved Truqap (capivasertib) in combination with abiraterone and prednisone as the first and only targeted treatment (company claim) for adults with PTEN-deficient metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive or sensitive prostate cancer (previously metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer), as detected by an FDA-authorised test; concurrently the FDA approved a companion diagnostic test to detect PTEN deficiency in prostate adenocarcinoma. The approval rests on the CAPItello-281 Phase III trial (1,012 patients): a statistically significant 19% reduction in the risk of radiographic disease progression or death (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.66-0.98; p=0.034), with median rPFS of 33.2 months versus 25.7 months (a 7.5-month improvement); overall survival was immature but numerically favoured the Truqap combination, and grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 67% of Truqap-combination patients. A regulatory application in this setting is under review in the EU. The company cites approximately 200,000 patients worldwide (35,000 in the US) diagnosed with this disease each year, one in four with PTEN-deficient tumours. It is Truqap's second tumour type after HR-positive breast cancer.
